title: Memory size and allocation: sizeof, malloc, and free

questions.prompt: Which option states the main idea of “Memory size and allocation: sizeof, malloc, and free” correctly?
options: Arduino `byte` is an alias for an unsigned 8-bit value from 0 to 255
RAM is the workbench used while a program runs: local variables usually live on the stack, while memory requested with `malloc`/`new` comes from the heap.
Everyday counting uses decimal, whose place weights are powers of 10.
questions.answer: RAM is the workbench used while a program runs: local variables usually live on the stack, while memory requested with `malloc`/`new` comes from the heap.
questions.explanation: RAM is the workbench used while a program runs: local variables usually live on the stack, while memory requested with `malloc`/`new` comes from the heap.

questions.prompt: Which additional fact about “Memory size and allocation: sizeof, malloc, and free” is accurate?
options: it is not a typed, scoped variable.
